decisions.reason: DCDC1 remains the primary 3.3V source when the power board is connected; the alternate USB LDO does not alter its stated normal-operation role or rating.
The source preserves AXP2101 as the normal-operation power source and introduces only a separate standalone-programming path when the power board is absent.
The standalone 3.3V LDO decision does not change the MT3608 enable control or its 5V loads; the source message's separate 5V clarification is already represented.
Using the main-board USB-C connector to activate the auxiliary supply does not change the selected connector, its data-line support, or its sourceability requirements.
The client explicitly establishes that main-board USB supports standalone programming while the power board is disconnected, adding an operational context to native USB flashing.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
3.3V rail (AXP2101 DCDC1, 2A) — primary power source when power board is connected:
\- ESP32-S3 module
\- INA219
\- All I2C sensors (SCD41, BME280, ENS160) via sensor board
\- I2C display
\- TTP223, AM312 PIR

5V rail (MT3608 boost, 500mA) — controlled by ESP32 GPIO3:
\- SPS30 particulate sensor
\- ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor
\- SK6812 LEDs (if wired to 5V — depends on version)

3.3V rail (ME6211A LDO, 1A) — only active when USB-C on main board connected WITHOUT power board:
\- Same 3.3V rail as above — Schottky diode OR-ing means whichever source is present wins. Used for standalone programming.

Battery (3.7–4.2V) — feeds AXP2101 which then feeds everything above.

Simple rule: in normal operation AXP2101 powers everything. The LDO only kicks in when programming without the power board connected.

decisions.reason: The conditional reference to SK6812 power does not identify the charge-status LED chain or change its display method, GPIO, or external LED interface.
The standalone supply operates when the power board is absent and does not change the legacy interboard connector partition, types, signals, or pin-order policy.
The main-board USB auxiliary supply does not alter the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, or mechanical placement requirements.
Supporting operation while the power board is disconnected does not remove that board or otherwise change the four-board project topology.
Changing which regulator supplies the shared 3.3V rail does not change the I2C speed, pull-up resistance and location, cable length, or series-resistor policy.
The source refers specifically to USB-C on the main board and does not alter power-board battery-connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source identifies I2C sensors as loads on the shared 3.3V rail but does not change the sensor board's connector-fanout role or define new port behavior.
